newsitem.title: UK: Grampian rebounds afer full-year results.
newsitem.headline: Grampian rebounds afer full-year results.

text.p: Shares in Grampian Television Plc rebounded from recent declines on Monday, after the company reported a 24 per cent increase in adjusted full year pre-tax profits, matching analyst expectations.

The shares gained 17-1/2p to 263-1/2p by 1418 GMT, after pre-tax profits for the year ended February 28 1997 came in at 11.82 million stg against 5.78 million stg for the previous year. The pre-tax figure included a 4.66 million contribution from the sale of SCOT FM.
Grampian shares dropped to a 12-month low of 243-1/2p at the end of last week.
Anthony de Larrinaga, media analyst at Panmure Gordon, said the stock looked good value after its recent decline.
"We have told clients that the shares are undervalued and have further to go," de Larrinaga said. "The stock has been oversold but is solidly based on fundamentals."
"Grampian has the added attraction of being a possible takeover target by Scottish Television," he added.
